Hieronymous Balbus represented Hungary at this meeting and unsuccessfully asked for help defending Belgrade from the Turks. Johann von Eck was the presiding officer at this event. Prior to this meeting, the bull Exurge Domine was issued by Leo X. One participant left this meeting in a burlap sack, as he had been kidnapped for his protection and taken to Wartburg by his supporter, Frederick the Wise of Saxony. This council condemned 41 beliefs as heretical and was called by a young Charles V. For 10 points name this 1521 council convoked to deal with that rascally Martin Luther.

This man was censured by his party for a militant speech in Sophiatown. Prior to being prosecuted, this man gave the "I am Prepared to Die" speech. He was one of the defendants at the "Treason Trial," where he was defended by Bram Fischer. Known for a time as the Black Pimpernel, he was put on trial at Rivona for his actions related to the Spear of the Nation movement, the military branch of his party. He was imprisoned on Robben Island until being released by F.W. De Klerk. Name this leader of the African National Congress, who fought for the end of apartheid before becoming president of South Africa.

During one set of peace negotiations, this man advocated a position of "no war, no peace," and after his policy was not listened to, he resigned in favor of Georgy Chicherin. This man's namesake ideology rejects the idea of historical stages and "socialism within one country" in favor of permanent revolution. During this man's exile in Coyoacan, he was attacked by Ramon Mercader with an ice pick. This man was tasked with forming and leading the Red Army during the Russian Civil War. Name this early Bolshevik who was ordered assassinated by Joseph Stalin.

During this man's administration, the Shufeldt Treaty with Korea was signed. This president signed the Edmunds Act, which prevented polygamists from holding office. Another piece of legislation enacted during his administration saw certain Asian immigrants denied citizenship via the Chinese Exclusion Act. This president upset his old mentor, Roscoe Conkling and his Stalwarts, by signing the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act, a piece of legislation prompted by the assassination of his predecessor by Charles Guiteau. Name this twenty-first President of the United States who succeeded James Garfield.

Some of this man's early partners were Benjamin Lundy and Isaac Knapp. He was sued for libel by Francis Todd because of what he wrote in his column "The Black List." He was succeeded as president of the organization he founded by Wendell Phillips. At an 1854 rally in Framingham, this man controversially burned a copy of the Constitution, calling it a "covenant with death." In the first issue of his newspaper, he proclaimed "I will not equivocate…I will not retreat a single inch—AND I WILL BE HEARD." name this founder of the American Anti-Slavery Society who also published the newspaper The Liberator.

This battle saw heroic action by the wounded General Philip Skippon, who refused to leave his post. Members of the losing side were butchered after getting trapped at the Marston Trussell church yard. At this battle, the Northern Horse faction was led by Marmaduke Langdale and served as the left wing cavalry unit for the Royalist army. Prince Rupert of the Rhine was driven from this battle by professional dragoons. Ending in a victory for the forces of Thomas Fairfax and Oliver Cromwell, for 10 points name this 1645 English Civil War battle, which saw the destruction of Charles I's army and was the first major victory for the New Model Army.

Count Miloradovich was murdered while attempting to negotiate with leaders of this event. Lieutenant Panov led an unsuccessful assault on the place during this event. This event was planned by the Union of Salvation. Pavel Pestel and Prince Troubetzkoy led this event's southern and northern factions. The northern leaders were attacked by artillery and forced to flee to the icy Neva River. Name this 1825 Russian rebellion whose participants demanded a constitution, in which numerous army officers pledged allegiance to Constantine instead of Nicholas I during a certain month.

As a child, this man was tutored by Hirate Masahide, who committed suicide after being shamed by this man's bad behavior. This commander defeated the Azai and Asakura clans at the Battle of Anegawa, while after this man's death, his opponents were defeated at the Battle of Yamazaki. This man destroyed a superior force from the rival Imagawa faction at the Battle of Okehazama. Akechi Mitsuhide betrayed this ruler at Honno-Ji, thereby causing him to commit suicide. Name this first unifier of Japan, later succeeded by such leaders as Tokugawa.

This collection points out that prosperity in commerce inevitably leads to war in a section that argues for the utility of economic unity. Under the pen name "Brutus", Robert Yates wrote a response to another essay in it that argues that documents like the Magna Carta ultimately threaten the freedom guaranteed by republican constitutions. This work that opposed the Bill of Rights contains another essay that argues for the double security provided by a system of checks and balances. Written under the pseudonym "Publius", name this collection of essays supporting the ratification of the Constitution by Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, and John Jay.

This figure's brother and wife Fulvia were defeated in a short lived war in the city of Perugia. This man was defeated at a battle which saw the deaths of the consuls Hirtius and Pansa. This figure was the father of Alexander Helios. While serving as Magister Equitum, this figure violently quelled a series of riots in Rome. This loser at the Battle of Mutina was the subject of Cicero's Philippics, and with the passage of the Lex Titia this man joined a group alongside Marcus Lepidus. Identify this figure who, with Octavian, won at the Battle of Philippi, but later lost at the Battle of Actium alongside Cleopatra.

One case during this man' s time as Chief Justice ruled that it was unconstitutional for the federal government to cancel one's citizenship as punishment. Another case during this man's tenure revolved around a break-in at a pool room in Florida. This man's court ruled that children at an Iowa school could wear black armbands as a sign of protest. The Chief Justice during such cases as Tinker v. Des Moines and Gideon v. Wainwright, this man wrote the majority opinion for the case which ruled "separate but equal" unconstitutional, Brown v. Board of Education. Name this liberal who served as Chief Justice from 1953 to 1969.

This ruler ordered the execution of Lucas Notaras, allegedly because of Notaras's opposition to pederasty. Alliances against this ruler include the League of Lezhe. At the Battle of Vaslui, Stephen the Great of Moldavia defeated this man. He defeated the White Sheep tribe and conquered the Despotate of Morea and the Empire of Trebizond. This ruler was the son of Murad II. In his most famous action, this he used logs to carry ships across the Golden Horn and made a mosque of the Hagia Sophia. Name this Ottoman sultan who captured Constantinople.

Under the 1606 Treaty of Vienna, a member of the Bocskay family with this first name became Prince of Transylvania. One king with this first name gained territory at the Treaty of Jam Zapolski, which he signed after defeating Ivan the Terrible. Besides the king who led Poland during the Livonian War, an English king with this name signed the Treaty of Winchester and succeeded Henry I. That king fought with Queen Maud during the Anarchy and was succeeded by Henry II Plantagenet. Give this name held by the only English king from the House of Blois.

A prince from this country apparently engaged in murder-suicide with his lover, Mary Vetsera, during the Mayerling Affair. One former leader of this country became head of the occupied Netherlands during World War II. A duke from this country held Richard the Lionheart hostage on his return from the Third Crusade. Its fascist movement was led by Engelbert Dolfuss and Kurt von Schussnig. It signed the Treaty of St. Germain after World War One and was the victim of the Anschluss. Name this Catholic, German-speaking country whose capital is Vienna.

Greek sources refer to this man as "Momylos," which means "Little Disgrace," and his house may have been converted into the tomb of St. Severinus. Primary evidence for this ruler's existence may include a letter written by Cassiodorus that might discuss this man's pension. This leader was the son of General Orestes, a former secretary to Attila the Hun. In his highest position, he succeeded Julius Nepos and had his court in Ravenna. The enemy who defeated this man was consequently appointed an administrator by Emperor Zeno. That enemy was Odoacer. Name this youth who briefly served as the last Roman Emperor.

The brothers Peter and Asen led a successful rebellion against this empire in one of its northern provinces. This Empire signed the Treaty of Devol. Its forces won the Battle of Dyrrhachium against Bohemund of Taranto, ending the Norman invasion of this empire. It lost to Alp Arslan's Seljuq forces at the Battle of Manzikert. Famous historians from this empire include the author of the Secret History, Procopius. This empire was home to the Nika Riot, and its most famous Emperor was married to Theodora. Name this empire ruled by Justinian, whose capital was Constantinople.

One incident during this event saw the fatal beating of Margaret Whitehead with a fence post. The instigators of this event were brutally suppressed by forces from the warships Warren and Natchez. Its leader interpreted a blue-green atmospheric disturbance as a sign of divine approval. Much of the information regarding it comes from a book written by Thomas Ruffin Gray, the court-appointed lawyer of this event's leader. After this action took place, Virginia passed a law heavily restricting the teaching of literacy to slaves. Name this 1831 uprising led by a slave known as the "Prophet," which resulted in the deaths of over fifty whites.

One daughter of this man married King Joao I of Portugal. Late in life, this man married his mistress, Katherine Swynford. He earlier married a Spanish princess after he intervened in a Spanish civil war and helped restore Pedro the Cruel to power. Residences of this man included the Savoy Palace, which was destroyed during the Watt Tyler riots. This man's brother was Edward the Black Prince, while his son defeated the Hotspur Rebellion and overthrew Richard II. Name this father of Henry IV, an English prince who founded the House of Lancaster.

According to some accounts, one incident which helped spark this event involved a deaf man who did not comprehend the orders to give up his gun. A court of inquiry investigated this event and exonerated Colonel James Forsyth of wrongdoing, much to the dismay of his superior General Nelson Miles. This event took place shortly after the surrender of Chief Big Foot. One precipitating cause was the teachings of Wovoka, whose preaching that the buffalo would return through Ghost Dancing alarmed the military. Name this 1890 incident in South Dakota where the U.S. Army massacred over hundred members of the Lakota Sioux.

This leader ordered the development of the Hotel and Golf class missile submarines. During the "Virgin Lands Program," this man attempted to plant corn in the tundra, leading to decreased agricultural production. During his leadership, the "Anti-Party Group" was purged. This man picked Janos Kadar as leader after crushing the revolt of Imre Nagy in Hungary. After the Cuban Missile Crisis, this man was replaced by Leonid Brezhnev. This man's notable speeches include the "Secret Speech", which condemned his predecessor in front of the Politburo. Name this leader of the Soviet Union who replaced Stalin.

In colonial times, this country was ruled by Lord Cromer, while the Milner Commission recommended changes in the administration of this nation. The Denshawai Incident took place in this country when British soldiers accidentally shot a local woman, helping to popularize the anti-British Wafd movement. In 1955, this country signed a notable arms deal with Communist Czechoslovakia. Its Free Officers Movement overthrew King Farouk in 1952. Name this country that signed the Camp David Accords with Israel, an Arab state ruled by Anwar Sadat and Gamal Nasser.

One figure from this city disguised himself as a peasant and picked a fight with a troop of Dorians. In addition to having leaders like Cylon and Codrus, this polity was briefly ruled by a group led by Critias and Theramenes called the Thirty Tyrants, and non-citizen residents of this city were known as metics. This city was led by commanders such as Nicias and Demosthenes in a conflict which saw the battle of Sphacteria, and later on this city was defeated by Lysander at the Battle of Aegospotami. Name this Greek city in Attica, the home of Peisistratus, Cleisthenes, and Pericles.

April Glaspie was one US ambassador to this man's regime, and one of this man's projects was destroyed in Operation Opera. As part of this his war against the Peshmerga, this man ordered the Halabja attack and the al-Anfal campaign. The Israeli-led Operation Opera stopped this man from building a nuclear reactor. He succeeded Ahmed al-Bakr, with whom he had led a coup to overthrow King Faisal II and put the Baath party in power. This man lost power in an invasion planned by Paul Wolfowitz and Donald Rumsfeld. Name this Iraqi dictator overthrown in 2003.

According to legend, an evil princess named Yodit once killed every member of this country's royal family and ruled for forty years. With the help of foreign musketeers, this country won the Battle of Wayna Daga, a victory over the Muslim Adal Empire. Yekuno Amlak overthrew this country's Zagwe dynasty. An era of instability in this country was called the "Age of the Princes" and was ended by Tewodros II. This country won the Battle of Adwa against Italy and its great rulers include Menelik II. Name this nation once ruled by Haile Selassie, with capital at Addis Ababa.

This navy failed to prevent amphibious invasions of its homeland during Operation Baytown and Operation Husky. In one conflict, its ship, the Ramb was destroyed by the New Zealand cruiser Leander. This navy first saw major action as an ally of Prussia during the Seven Weeks War. This navy was defeated by Admiral Tegetthoff at the Battle of Lissa in 1866, and was attacked by Admiral Miklos Horthy during the Battle of the Otranto Barage in World War I, both of which were battles this navy fought against Austria in the Adriatic Sea. Name this navy whose ships included the Marco Polo and Leonardo Da Vinci and which was based in Rome.

Ignatius White was a diplomat who attempted to convince France to oppose this event. Support for this event was drummed up by Hans Bentick. This event was planned and favored by Henry Sydney, who led the "Immortal Seven." This event saw the calling of the "Convention Parliament," and it was sparked by fears that the son of Mary of Modena would inherit the throne. Supporters of this event took the name "Whigs" and favored property rights while opposing Catholicism. For 10 points name this 1688 event that replaced James II of England with William and Mary.

This man rallied a Yale student militia to defend a British assault on New Haven. This man asked for monetary assistance from the Marqués de Casa Irujo and mustered his forces on Blennerhassett Island. Eventually, he informed General James Wilkinson of his plan to invade Mexico. Acquitted of treason at his trial, this man had earlier presided over the impeachment of Samuel Chase. He enlisted Tammany Hall to win Thomas Jefferson the state of New York in 1800 and received an equal number of electoral votes in the election, forcing the House to choose a winner. Name this Vice-President who killed Alexander Hamilton in a duel.

As a general, this man defeated the Durotriges while in command of the second legion. He executed Helvidius Priscus for his staunch defense of the Senate's power and appointed Gnaeus Agricola to a seven-year governorship of Britain. His generals included Gaius Licinius Mucianus, who stopped the Great Jewish Revolt, and Antonius Primus, who helped this man defeat Vitellus to become emperor. Name this founder of the Flavian dynasty who started building the Colosseum and was succeeded by Titus and Domitian, the final victor in the Year of the Four Emperors.

One controversy during this battle was the tardy appearance of General Lew Wallace, who had led his troops down the wrong road. Near the end of this battle, the losing side's calvary under Nathan Bedford Forrest mounted a wild counter-charge at a site called "Fallen Timbers." P.G.T. Beauregard took command of the losing side after his superior, Albert Sidney Johnston, was slain. This battle saw sieges of the Union positions at the Hornet's Nest and later at Pittsburg Landing, which is an alternate name for this battle. Name this key 1862 victory for Ulysses S. Grant in southwestern Tennessee, the bloodiest two-day battle of the Civil War.

This man won his first election in the constituency of Maidstone and once appointed R.A. Cross to spearhead reforms intended to help the working class. This man served as Foreign Minister to the Earl of Derby, whom he succeeded as Prime Minister. He was defeated in the Midlothian Campaign, in part because he did not stop the Bulgarian Horrors. This politician notably attended the Congress of Berlin and lost the first election after the Reform Act of 1867. Name this Victorian Prime Minister from the Conservative party, a rival of Gladstone, whose name reflects his Jewish ancestry.

During this man's reign, the empire he ruled was expanded by the general Sagmandia. This ruler briefly lost control of his capital to an invasion by the Mossi peoples. He ruler hired the architect Abu Ishaq es Saheli to build structures such as the Hall of Audience, Sankore University, and the Djinguereber Mosque. This man was succeeded by King Maghan and was part of the Kieta dynasty. A collapse in the price of gold was one consequence of his famous hajj to Mecca. Name this most famous king of Mali.

National heroes in this country include the gay Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa [nop-cha], who helped lead its independence movement and wanted to become its first king. The 1924 "June Revolution" in this country was led by Bishop Fan Noli, who briefly served as Prime Minister. Hundreds of concrete pillboxes were built by this country's Communist rulers, who included Ramiz Alia. These leaders were protected by the Sigurimi secret police. Name this once-Maoist Balkan country of Enver Hoxha and King Zog, whose languages are Gheg and Tosk and whose capital is Tirana.

During one debate during this election, the Democratic candidate was asked how he would feel about capital punishment if his wife were raped and murdered. At the Democratic convention before this election, Ann Richards said the Republican nominee was born with a "silver foot in his mouth." The Republican candidate successfully used the image of black convict Willie Horton against his opponent. During the vice presidential debate, Lloyd Bentsen said his Republican counterpart was "no Jack Kennedy." name this presidential election which saw a man who promised "no new taxes," George H.W. Bush, defeat Michael Dukakis.

The early rulers of this city were members of the Bacchiad family ending with Telestes. A war named for this city concluded with the Peace of Antalcidas and saw the battles of Nemea and Coronea against the Spartan king Agesilaus II. This city was ruled by the tyrants Cypselus and Periander, and this its colonies included Corcyra and Syracuse. Philip II founded a League named for this place after destroying the Theban Sacred Band at the Battle of Charonea, and this city was razed by the Romans under Lucius Mummius in 146 B.C.E. Name this Greek city state located on a namesake isthmus.

This polity rose to prominence after the collapse of the neighboring Pallava empire. One ruler of this polity built the Brihadeeswarar temple. This polity collapsed due to a rebellion of their Pandyan vassals, and late in its existence it was a rival of the Hoysala Empire. Many rulers of this polity were named Rajendra or Rajaraja. This empire notably expanded to include the Malay Peninsula and parts of modern Indonesia, but was based in Tamil-speaking areas. Name this empire based around the Kaveri River, the most important empire in South India.

This battle saw heroic action by the wounded General Philip Skippon, who refused to leave his post. At this battle, the Northern Horse faction was led by Marmaduke Langdale and served as the left wing cavalry unit for the Royalist army. Prince Rupert of the Rhine was driven from this battle by professional dragoons. Ending in a victory for the forces of Thomas Fairfax and Oliver Cromwell, for ten points name this 1645 English Civil War battle, which saw the destruction of Charles I's army and was the first major victory for the New Model Army.

The end of this event became known as "the Bloody Week." During this event, Generals Lecomte and Thomas were executed after attempting to prevent artillery from being stockpiled on top of Montmartre Hill. Leaders of this event took Bishop Goerge Darboy hostage and attempted to exchange him for Louis Blanqui. During this event, the Vendome Column was destroyed and military power was placed in the hands of General Jaroslaw Dabrowski. Eventually put down by the nationalist government of Adolphe Thiers, for 10 points name this socialist government in France formed after the Franco-Prussian War, which briefly ruled out of the capital in 1871.

As the governor of Cilicia, this man was the first Roman official to meet with a Parthian ambassador, and he served under Quintus Catulus in defeating the Cimbri at the Battle of Vercellae. His victories at Orchomenos and Chaeronea over Archelaus led to the end of the Mithridatic War, after which he turned his attention to a Rome led by Cinna. In his most famous post, he greatly reduced the power of the Tribunes and strengthened the Senate, depite executing 1,500 nobles. With the help of King Bocchus, he captured Jugurtha, although credit was given to his superior and rival. Name this Roman general, the enemy of Marius.

One force failed to arrive at this event because it was held up in the Baro Gorge. That force was led by Christian de Bonchamps. Gabriel Hanotaux had ordered Jean-Baptiste Marchand to march to this event, though those orders were rescinded by Theophile Delcasse, who became foreign minister during this event. Another force arrived at this event after winning the Battle of Omdurman and was led by Herbert Kichener. Name this 1898 incident that saw heightened tensions between the French and British over colonial claims on the namesake Sudanese town.

This figure was the titular subject of a tragedy written by British soldier Robert Rogers, while historian Francis Parkman wrote of The Conspiracy of this man. After his forces killed Captain James Dalyell, General Jeffrey Amherst placed a 200-pound bounty on this man's head. The victor at the Battle of Bloody Run, this leader was eventually slain at Cahokia by a member of the rival Peoria tribe. The conflict associated with this man saw the bloody actions of the Paxton Boys and the sieges of both Fort Miami and Fort Pitt. Name this Ottawa chief who launched a 1763 war against the British and who personally laid siege to Fort Detroit.

The Kania government was overthrown in a military coup after deciding to negotiate with this organization. This organization first emerged to oppose the budget cuts of Edward Gierek. Under one compromise, the government bought leaders of this group one-way tickets out of the country. This group engaged in the Round Table Talks with General Jaruzelski. Agitation from this group eventually led to free elections, leading to this group's leader becoming President and winning the Nobel Peace Prize. Name this group led by Lech Walesa, which opposed Communism in 1980's Poland.

This man was the nominal commander of 6,000 militiamen assigned to assist John Sullivan during the failed Newport assault. The British ship Romney seized his sloop, the Liberty, eventually leading to a trial where this man was defended by James Otis. After the Revolution, this man resigned his position and was replaced by James Bowdoin, who had to deal with Shays' Rebellion. Mentored by Samuel Adams, this man was president of the Second Continental Congress in 1776, which allowed him to complete his most remembered act. Name this first governor of Massachusetts, noted for his large signature on the Declaration of Independence.

Giovanni Vilani recorded the history of this city in a work called Cronica nuova. Giano della Bella led a movement against the nobles of this city which resulted in the 1293 Ordinances of Justice. This polity defeated the Republic of Siena at the Battle of Marciano, and early in the fourteenth century, the Peruzzi family dominated politics in this city. This city also saw a revolt by oppressed wool-workers, called the Ciompi revolt. Two other rulers of this city were targets of the Pazzi conspiracy. Identify this Italian city, which was once ruled by Cosimo and Lorenzo of the Medici family.

During this decade, an international border along the Arta-Volos line was recognized by the London Convention, and Stratford Canning negotiated the Treaty of Constantinople. During this decade, William Sleeman began his campaign to wipe out the Thuggee cult in India, while the Kowloon Incident kicked off the First Opium War. British Prime Ministers from this decade include Lord Melbourne and the Earl Grey. The first year of this decade saw Charles X toppled by the July Revolution, which brought Louis-Philippe to power in France. Name this decade, the fourth of the nineteenth century.

This man's only Supreme Court appointment was that of his Naval Secretary, Smith Thompson. While this man was president, the Choctaw chief Pushmataha ceded territory to the U.S. In the Treaties of Doak's Stand and Washington City. Another treaty during his presidency established the Sabine and Red Rivers as borders with New Spain and ceded Florida to the U.S. That treaty, the Adams-Onis Treaty, was negotiated by this man's Secretary of State, John Quincy Adams. Upon the collapse of the Federalists, this man ran for reelection unopposed. Name this fifth U.S. President, whose namesake doctrine told Europe to stay out of American affairs.

Participants in this event used a rectangular red flag with a black square in the middle. The Hanlin Academy caught fire during this event, leading to a dramatic rescue of the sole surviving copy of the Yongle Encyclopedia. Claude MacDonald used the "International Gun" to defend his men during it, while the Taiyuan Massacre also occurred during this event. The instigators of this event objected to the granting of extraterritoriality by the unequal treaties. This event during the Qing Dynasty was eventually put down by an Eight-Nation Alliance that included Japan, Britain, and the United States. Name this 1899-1901 anti-foreigner rebellion in China.

Advisers to this king included Ruy Gomez. The right of this man to rule was rejected by the Act of Abjuration, and alliances against this king include the Union of Utrecht. He conquered a neighboring country whose throne had gone vacant because of the Battle of Alcacer Quibir, after which this man became King of Portugal. One plan hatched by this king involved the land forces of Alexander Farnese being ferried by the sea forces of the Duke of Medina-Sidonia, but these were foiled by Sir Francis Drake. Name this King of Spain who launched the Spanish Armada.

One man to hold this title worked with Commodore Matthew Maury to create the New Virginia Colony. Another man who held this title led the "Army of the Three Guarantees" after signing an agreement with his rival, Vicente Guerrero. One holder of this title was captured at Queretaro and executed at the Hill of the Bells after being defeated by General Porfirio Diaz and President Benito Juarez. That man was the husband of Carlotta. Name this title held by Agustin Iturbide from 1822-1823 and Maximillian von Habsburg from 1864-1867, which involves reigning over America's southern neighbor.

This king defeated Widukind, who led a guerilla war against this man in Saxony. He outlawed Jewish money-lending in his Capitulary for the Jews. In another war, this man defeated King Desiderius, his former father-in-law. This man ordered the beheading of 4,000 Saxons for practicing paganism in the Massacre of Verden. Important court scholars to this king included Alcuin of York. Biographers of this man include Einhard. He defeated the Lombards, who were threatening to seize Rome, thus earning the gratitude of Pope Leo III, who crowned him on Christmas Day in 800. Name this King of the Franks known as "the Great."

A political leader in this state was Herman Husband, who opposed Governor William Tryon. A Supreme Court case associated with this state affirmed that Judge James McMillan's order for busing to achieve racial integration was constitutional. It was the home of the 1771 Battle of Alamance, which put down a rebellion against colonial taxation. It saw a bloody Revolutionary War battle at Guilford Court House and was the site of the Swann case and the War of the Regulation. In 1960, this state saw the first sit-in demonstration at a Woolworth's lunch counter. Name this Southern state with such cities as Greensboro and Charlotte.

This man met with Army Secretary Robert Stevens in what would be called the "Chicken Luncheon." He was heavily criticized for his defense of the SS soldiers accused of perpetrating the Malmedy massacre. This man was later investigated by the Watkins Committee, and he was earlier rebuked by the Tydings Committee. This politician's downfall came after he was notably criticized by attorney Joseph Welch. In 1950, this man gave a speech in Wheeling, West Virginia, where he claimed to have an infamous list. Name this Wisconsin Senator whose name is synonymous with the 1950's "witch-hunting" of Communists in the government.

Participants in this event opposed the corrupt "Ten Regular Attendants." He Jin led the military opposition to this event, while forces under Bo Cai were put down by Zhu Jun and Huangfu Song. Participants in this event believed that "the Blue Sky" had perished and venerated the god Huang-lo, who had given its leader a sacred book. That leader's brothers Bao and Liang helped him lead this rebellion, which, like the earlier Five Pecks of Rice revolt, was put down by the Han general Cao Cao. Name this Zhang Jiao-led uprising against the Han Dynasy whose followers practiced the Way of Great Peace and were named after a colorful piece of headware.

Count von Cobenzl was fired as foreign minister after this battle. This battle resulted in a treaty signed in the Primate's Palace in Bratislava, the Treaty of Pressburg. The winning commander at this battle defied convention by dividing his army against a numerically superior force and choosing to fight from the low ground. This battle ended with the taking of the Pratzen Heights, and saw the losers retreat over a frozen lake. Name this greatest victory of Napoleon Bonaparte, where he routed the combined forces of Alexander I of Russia and Francis II of Austria, which led to its alternate name of "Battle of the Three Emperors."

In the Republican primaries prior to this presidential election, Henry Cabot Lodge Jr. Won the New Hampshire primary on a write-in vote organized by amateurs on a whim without Lodge's support. The controversial film Choice was made to promote the losing candidacy in this election. At the Democratic convention, Fannie Lou Hamer and other Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party delegates attempted to be seated. During this election, Ronald Reagan achieved national prominence by giving his "A Time for Choosing" speech in support of the losing candidate. This election saw the first Republican victories in the Deep South since Reconstruction and the losing candidate in this election was maligned for making statements like "Extremism in the defense of liberty is no vice," and was painted as a warmonger by the famous "Daisy" TV advertisement. Name this election year in which Lyndon Johnson retained the presidency by thrashing Barry Goldwater.

This empire battled the rebellious forces of Saint Vartan in the Battle of Avaryr and lost the Battle of the Chains. In this empire's waning days, it won the Battle of the Bridge, but was finally obliterated in the "victory of victories" called the Battle of Nahavand. One ruler of this empire was crowned in utero by having a crown placed on his mother's stomach. The emperor Maurice married off his daughter Miriam to one ruler of this empire and also helped oust a usurper named Bahram Chobin. Julian the Apostate died while fighting this empire, as part of its incessant conflicts with Roman and Byzantine forces. This empire eventually collapsed after forces of the Arab Caliphs seized its capital, Ctesiphon, in the early 637. Founded by Ardashir I, name this empire ruled by guys like Khosrau and Shapur, the last non-Islamic empire to rule Persia.

A campaign two years prior to this battle saw one the combatants force the capitulation of Alexander I of Macedon and conquer Thrace. This battle was immediately preceded by the sack of Naxos and the siege of Eritrea. A famous anecdote about this battle tells of how Cynaegirus tried to bring one of the loser's ships back to shore by latching onto its prow. The winning side attempted to delay this battle since their allies were in the middle of a ten day festival called the Carneia. Though the polemarch, Callimachus commanded the right wing on the winning side and the forces of Datis and Artaphernes were pushed back to their ships by a charge led by another strategos, Militiades. Phidippides was sent on a 26 mile run to report an Atheinan victory at, what 490 BC battle that brought Darius' invasion of Greece to an end.

The beginning of this man's term saw the passage of the Badinter Act, which abolished the death penalty. Originally a supporter of Petain, this future interior minister of USDR broke with the Vichy government over Pierre Laval's decision to send French workers to Germany. He issued sweeping labor reforms that increased minimum wage by 10% and instituted a shorter work week.
